Every clause of that is now false. The design mission `m-2026-08-30-053` closed with verdict pass. The follow-on implementation mission `m-2026-08-31-002` also closed pass. And this very PR carries the implementation — the harness, the fixtures, the CI wiring, and the `docs/TESTING.md` tier.

- **Don't leave a status line that will rot again.** This document has already been bitten three separate times by claims that were true when written and false weeks later — decayed line-number citations, a stale `v4.15.0` pin, and a `t.Skip` count that was wrong by 3.5x and had been copied twice before anyone counted. Prefer phrasing anchored to facts that don't drift (mission IDs, a PR number) over anything that needs updating as the code evolves. If you find yourself writing a number or a date that will need maintenance, that's a signal to phrase it differently.
- **Check the rest of the document for the same staleness.** Grep for other "proposed", "will", "follow-on", "this design will", or future-tense framing that described intent at authoring time and now describes shipped work. Report what you find and fix it, or say "nothing further" if the header is the only instance. Don't rewrite substance — the design's decisions are ratified and binding; only correct tense and status.

Run markdownlint. Commit. Do not push — return to me with the new header text and your sweep results.
